1.0.0.en: The word of the LORD which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah. [1]

1.0.1.en: The introduction to the book confirms that what the prophet Zephaniah records is not his own words, but the word of the Lord, declared to him from heaven.

1.0.2.en: He gives us the family tree back four generations, ending with King Hezekiah, who is mentioned in Second Kings (2 Kgs 18:1).

1.0.3.en: Josiah began the movement of reform in the twelfth year of his reign; so if the prophet Zephaniah began his prophecy at the beginning of Josiah's reign, then he certainly had his principal part in the movement of reform.

1.0.4.en: We should not wonder at the prophet's insistence on mentioning Amon, the idol worshiper, from whose offspring came Josiah, who did all that was in his power for religious and spiritual reform. On the one hand he wished to confirm the gravity of evil. For with all the effort that Josiah made, the people were as in an incurable sickness, since corruption had grown rampant among them because of Amon. On the other hand he wished to open before us the door of hope, for if the father was corrupt, as one from whom no good is expected, the young son defied the corruption of his father and set out to work in the spirit of power. And as the Lord Himself declares through Ezekiel the responsibility of every man for his own conduct, not for the deserts of his father: "Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die" (Ezek 18:4). "Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father's sins, which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like... he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live" (Ezek 18:14, 17).

1.0.5.en: * The soul that does not dwell in God is the source of its own evils, so it sins, and the soul that sins itself dies.

1.1.0.en: 2 "I will utterly consume all things from off the land, saith the LORD. 3 I will consume man and beast; I will consume the fowls of the heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumblingblocks with the wicked; and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the LORD. 4 I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with the priests; 5 And them that worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and them that worship and that swear by the LORD, and that swear by Malcham; 6 And them that are turned back from the LORD; and those that have not sought the LORD, nor enquired for him."

1.1.1.en: I will utterly consume all things from off the land, saith the LORD. [2]

1.1.2.en: God created the earth that man might enjoy it as His ambassador and steward of heaven, so that the earth might be the icon of heaven; but now that man has become corrupt, God removes this earth from existence. For sin has corrupted man as it has corrupted the earth on which he lives. Moreover, the heavenly Word of God came down to our earth, to raise up from our hearts a second heaven, made fit by His grace for His dwelling. So he who insists on remaining earth and dust does not deserve to remain, but hears the divine voice: "I will utterly consume all things from off the land" [1]. But if we become heaven, we live with the Apostle Paul in the heavenly places; we are not removed, but enjoy the divine embraces eternally.

1.1.3.en: Thus as long as man insists on remaining earthy (of the earth), he drinks the golden cup of the bitterness of sin, so he becomes drunk and loses his balance, indeed his whole life. Therefore it is fitting for us to ask God to remove from our hearts everything that is earthly.

1.1.4.en: * "Babylon hath been a golden cup in the LORD'S hand, that made all the earth drunken" (Jer 28:7)... If you wish to know how all the earth has become drunken by the cup of Babylon, look at the sinners who fill the whole earth. But you may say to me that the righteous have not become drunken from the cup of sinners, so how does Scripture say that all the earth is made drunken from the cup of Babylon? Do not think that Scripture does not speak the truth when it says this, for the righteous in fact are not earth (dust), and therefore only all the earth, that is, the sinners alone, are those who become drunken. As for the righteous, although they are on the earth, their dwelling is in the heavens (Phil 3:20). Therefore it is not fitting that the righteous man should be told: "Thou art earth (dust), and unto earth (dust) shalt thou return," but the Lord will say to him, as long as that man wears the image of the heavenly (1 Cor 15:49): "Thou art heaven, and unto heaven shalt thou return." Therefore the cup of Babylon will not make drunken any but those who are still earth.

1.1.5.en: Origen I will consume man and beast.

1.2.0.en: I will consume the fowls of the heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumblingblocks with the wicked; and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the LORD. [3]

1.2.1.en: He removes man and beast, either by captivity or by plagues that destroy them; and the air is corrupted until the fowls of the heaven die, and the waters are also corrupted so that the fishes of the sea die.

1.2.2.en: The Lord depicts the complete desolation that befalls mankind who deny their Creator, for He removes man and beast. If man signifies the rational human soul and the beast the animal body, then sin destroys the life of man as a whole: it deprives him of his rational nature, and it shatters his body as he thinks his happiness is in bodily pleasures.

1.2.3.en: He removes the fowls of the heaven and the fishes of the sea, for if man thinks that he is able to fly as though to heaven, or descend as though to the depths of the sea with the fishes, he will not be able to hide from the eye of God, nor to flee from the divine chastening, as the psalmist says: "Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there..." (Ps 139:7-8). It is fitting for him to flee not from God but to God Himself.

1.2.4.en: * Where shall the slave of sin flee? For he carries (his mistress, that is, sin) wherever he flees.

1.2.5.en: The evil conscience does not flee from itself; there is no place for it to go to.

1.2.6.en: Indeed it cannot withdraw from itself, for the sin it commits is within it. It commits sin in order to obtain some bodily pleasure. But the pleasure passes and the sin remains. What it delights in passes, and the thorn remains behind it. What an evil slavery...!

1.2.7.en: Let us all flee to Christ, and protest against sin to God as our Savior.

1.2.8.en: * He seeks a place to which he may flee from the wrath of God. What place protects the one who flees from God...? What place is there in which God is not? Who can deceive God? Who is there that God does not see?

1.2.9.en: * Let us flee in hope and longing on the wings of the double love (the love of God and the love of neighbor), so that we find no rest except in the depths of the sea (of love)... Let us flee to God in hope, and in a hope filled with faith let us contemplate at the end of the sea.

1.3.0.en: St. Augustine I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with the priests. [4]

1.3.1.en: Since some thought that God would not permit the desolation of Judah because of the presence of the city of God, Jerusalem, and the Temple, the holy God declares that what concerns Him is neither Jerusalem nor the Temple as a building, but holiness, which He desires for all mankind; if men lose the holy life, He is ready to remove the whole earth with all that is on it, which He created for the sake of man.

1.3.2.en: If God stretches out His hand to chasten Judah in general, He chastens all the more Jerusalem, which was consecrated as the city of God containing the holy Temple, because she permitted the mixing of the worship of God with pagan worship. He declared that He will cut off the name of Baal and his worship from the land, and the Chemarims [priests of the idols (2 Kgs 23:5)] who were leading the people astray. He cuts them off with their idols, and also cuts off those who worship the stars, and those who swear by the name of Malcham.

1.3.3.en: "Baal" is the Phoenician guardian god. Israel fell into this pagan worship from the time of the judges (Judg 2:13). King Manasseh set up an image of Baal in the Temple itself (2 Kgs 21:3, 5, 7).

1.3.4.en: Chemarim: the Hebrew origin is derived from a word whose meaning is "black," since the priests wore black garments and also placed a black mark on their foreheads. Some think that the priests of Molech were called the black men because of the continual smoke that rose from the altar on which they burned human sacrifices, where some offered their children as sacrifices. So the faces of the priests were black. The word chemarim also means "jealousy," because of their fanaticism and their zeal for spreading paganism.

1.4.0.en: And them that worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and them that worship and that swear by the LORD, and that swear by Malcham. [5]

1.4.1.en: God rejects the mixing of what belongs to God with what belongs to the devil, and the fellowship between light and darkness. For when a part of the heart is surrendered to the devil, he storms it to reign over it completely, and if a part of the heart is left to God, He rejects it completely and departs from it. The devil by his deceit creeps in to reign completely, and God in His love will not force Himself in unless the heart is completely surrendered to Him that He may set up His Kingdom in it.

1.4.2.en: Some were accustomed to mixing the worship of the living God with the worship of idols, and to adding to their oath by the living God the name or names of pagan gods.

1.4.3.en: The worship of the sun or the moon or one of the stars was a common thing, and is among the oldest of pagan worships.

1.5.0.en: And them that are turned back from the LORD; and those that have not sought the LORD, nor enquired for him. [6]

1.5.1.en: Here he divides the people into two groups: one group responded to the call of King Josiah to repentance, but only for a time, then turned back from the LORD to practice pagan abominations. These put their hands to the plough and looked back. As for the second group, they did not respond to the call of the king, and the Lord did not concern them at all.

1.5.2.en: The book concentrates on three main errors, which are: 1. The worship of idols [4-5]. 2. Halting between the two parties, at one time swearing by the living God and at another by Malcham [5]. 3. Turning the back to God [6].

1.6.s.en: 3. The day of the Lord is near:

1.6.0.en: 7 "Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD: for the day of the LORD is at hand: for the LORD hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests. 8 And it shall come to pass in the day of the LORD'S sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king's children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel. 9 In the same day also will I punish all those that leap on the threshold, which fill their masters' houses with violence and deceit. 10 And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and an howling from the second, and a great crashing from the hills. 11 Howl, ye inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the people of Canaan are cut down; all they that bear silver are cut off. 12 And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil. 13 Therefore their goods shall become a booty, and their houses a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof."

1.6.1.en: Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD: for the day of the LORD is at hand.

1.6.2.en: For the LORD hath prepared a sacrifice.

1.6.4.en: Since many mocked the words of the prophets that threatened the destruction of Jerusalem, saying that generation after generation had passed and nothing of this had happened, and that the prophets were threatening what would never be fulfilled, the prophet Zephaniah says: "The day of the LORD is at hand" [7].

1.6.5.en: The present time is regarded as the days of men, who do as they please, but the last day, when God proclaims His eternal Kingdom and gathers to Himself His true believers, is the day of the Lord, and every man is judged according to his works. The weekly day of worship is also regarded as the day of the Lord, when the believer consecrates this day to worship that it may be a mystery of blessing for the whole week. Also the day of chastening that is accomplished in this age, at the time appropriate for each one, is counted as the day of the Lord, and it is near.

1.6.6.en: He permitted the Babylonians to kill and slaughter the Jews when they triumphed over Judah, and these slain were counted as though they were a sacrifice offered by the priests to the Lord. Here the prophet depicts their slaughter in bitterness: they are killed without mercy and without stirring of conscience, but their killers count them a sacrifice offered to the Lord! They exult and rejoice while killing them by offering human sacrifices as on a day of feast.

1.6.7.en: The word of the Lord came describing that day: "For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord GOD of hosts hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates" (Jer 46:10). It was also said: "And thou, son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood. Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth" (Ezek 39:17-18).

1.7.0.en: And it shall come to pass in the day of the LORD'S sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king's children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel. [8]

1.7.1.en: When the Lord chastens His people He begins with the princes and the king's children and the nobles, and the leaders like them, as with the rest of the sinning classes, without partiality.

1.7.2.en: Since God permitted Nebuchadnezzar to slaughter the wicked great men of Judah, offering them as a sacrifice, he began with the princes or the rulers, for they ought to have been an example to the people, but they became a stumblingblock to them. This prophecy was fulfilled when the sons of Zedekiah were killed (Jer 39:6).

1.7.3.en: "All such as are clothed with strange apparel" means the princes and the men of the court who wore garments imported from abroad, very costly, as a kind of luxury and grandeur; and perhaps these garments belonged to the pagans, who made a show of them during pagan worship. By wearing these garments they were counted as having shared in pagan worship. Some think that the strange garments are those that the Law forbade, such as men wearing women's garments, and the reverse also (Deut 22:5).

1.8.0.en: In the same day also will I punish all those that leap on the threshold, which fill their masters' houses with violence and deceit. [9]

1.8.1.en: "Those that leap on the threshold": an expression that usually means a man's assault on the rights of his neighbor, like one who leaps over the threshold to seize something from his neighbor's house by violence as well as by deceit.

1.8.2.en: Some think that it means here those who flatter the royal court, where they were seizing what belonged to others for their masters, so they are like hunting dogs that leap over the threshold to seize the property of others for the men of the palace. Others see in it a reference to the Philistines, who seized the ark of God and brought it to Ashdod, and entered with it into the house of Dagon and set it beside the god Dagon; and when the latter fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the covenant, with his head and his hands cut off on the threshold, the priests and all who entered used to leap so as not to tread on the threshold with their feet, and this became a custom for all who enter the temple of Dagon (1 Sam 5:1-5). St. Jerome sees that it refers here to those who go up the steps of the Temple in haughtiness and pride.

1.9.0.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and an howling from the second, and a great crashing from the hills. [10]

1.9.1.en: The fish gate: this gate is mentioned in Nehemiah (Neh 3:3); it is opposite Joppa, and perhaps it is the gate from which came the news of the violent storming of the Chaldean army from the region of the hills. It was called the fish gate because of its nearness to the fish market, and because the fishermen coming from the Lake of Tiberias and the River Jordan used to pass through this gate.

1.9.2.en: When the cry arose from the fish gate, the reaction was in the second quarter or the lower part of the city, where they howled on hearing the cries that were coming.

1.9.3.en: When the cries resounded around the walls of Jerusalem, coming from the surrounding mountains, resounding from gate to gate, surely despair befell all the inhabitants in the safest regions.

1.9.4.en: Howl, ye inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the people of Canaan are cut down.

1.10.0.en: All they that bear silver are cut off. [11]

1.10.1.en: Evil was found in Maktesh, in a low and deep place in the city, like a mortar. The merchants and businessmen dwelt there at ease, but desolation befell them, and there was no longer any bearer of silver or money entering for trade! Its people became ground, as wheat or medicine is ground in a mortar. In the Book of Ezekiel He likens it to the pot into which every good piece is put: the thigh and the shoulder with the choice bones, and He boils it until its bones are also seethed in the midst of it (Ezek 24:3-5).

1.10.2.en: Some think that it refers here not to a particular location in Jerusalem but to the whole city, where the people are struck and crushed to death like wheat in the mortar.

1.10.3.en: Maktesh or Mortar, that is, a mortar; it is a name that applies to the valley of Siloam by its hollow shape. This valley is between Zion and Mount Olivet at the extreme eastern side of Mount Moriah, where the merchants dwell. Perhaps it was near the fish gate.

1.10.4.en: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart,

1.11.0.en: The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil. [12]

1.11.1.en: When some see the righteous in distress while the wicked enjoy success and prosperity, they often ask: Where is divine justice? Where is the reward that the righteous receive? And where is the punishment that befalls the wicked? Where is God's care and concern for mankind?

1.11.2.en: Here God, as He chastens Jerusalem for her evils, is pictured holding candles, searching even in the hidden, dark places, that no wicked man may escape the divine chastening. Here the Lord searches Jerusalem with candles not to look for the lost piece of silver (Lk 15:8-10), for He has given the sinners many opportunities to return to Him; therefore He uses the candles to single out the wicked who insist on despising God's warnings, in order to chasten them.

1.11.3.en: God punishes not only those who become drunk with the wine of the love of luxury and the world, but even those who drink what remains of the sediment in the wine bottles (the dregs). These in their drunkenness fall into practical atheism, where they do not deny the existence of God, but deny His providence over the world or His concern for mankind, as though man does not concern Him at all.

1.11.4.en: In this chapter the Lord appears as one who is in the midst of Judah to judge her or chasten her, but in the last chapter He announces His dwelling in the midst of mankind that she may rejoice in Him as He delights in her, for she is the place of His pleasure. Here He announces His chastening of Judah, which worships idols, a thing that God cannot bear in His people.

1.11.5.en: * The Lord Jesus came to Jerusalem, into the Temple. And when he had looked round about upon all things, and now the eventide was come, he went out unto Bethany with the twelve (Mk 11:11). The Lord entered Jerusalem, into the Temple. And when He entered, what did He do? He looked round about upon all things. He was in the temple of the Jews seeking a place to lay His head, and found none...

1.11.6.en: He looked at the Jews; and He wished to be in their midst, but He did not find them...

1.11.7.en: He was assessing everything around Him like one searching with a candle, therefore the prophet Zephaniah says: "I will search Jerusalem with candles" (Zeph 1:12).

1.11.8.en: In the same way the Lord also looked around Him upon all things by the light of a candle. He was searching in the Temple and did not find what He sought, until evening came and He was still examining everything... As long as there was light, He remained in the Temple. But when evening had come, when the shadows of ignorance had fallen, so the temple of the Jews became dark, He went out to Bethany with the twelve.

1.11.9.en: The Savior searched, and the Apostles searched, and when they found nothing in the Temple they left it.

1.11.10.en: St. Jerome * This question is often repeated in the minds of those who do not have great faith and knowledge, thinking that the reward of the saints, which is not given in this world but in the life to come, is granted to them in this short period of transient life. But we have set our hope in Christ, not in this life, lest we become, as the Apostle says, of all men most miserable (1 Cor 15:19).

1.11.11.en: For God does not keep trials away from the upright, nor does He reward in this world the righteous with profitable things and the wicked with evil things.

1.11.12.en: If we say otherwise, we fall into punishment with those whom the prophet Zephaniah mentions: "that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil" (Zeph 1:12). Or at the least we become among the blasphemers against God who say: "Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delighteth in them; or, Where is the God of judgment?" (Mal 2:17), and we fall into the blasphemy that he (the prophet) described thus: "Ye have said, It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts? And now we call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up; yea, they that tempt God are even delivered" (Mal 3:14-15).

1.12.0.en: Father Theodore Therefore their goods shall become a booty, and their houses a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof. [13]

1.12.1.en: Although God in His long-suffering does not hasten to impose punishment on the wicked, waiting for their repentance through His tenderness toward them, yet surely if they do not return they will drink from the cup that they have filled.

1.12.2.en: The enemy strips them of everything, of their wealth, and of their houses that are the work of their hands, as well as of their vineyards that they planted, for the invaders seize everything. Thus the prophecy recorded in (Deut 28:30, 39) is fulfilled concerning the one who does not hearken to the voice of the Lord: "Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof... Thou shalt plant vineyards, and dress them, but shalt neither drink of the wine, nor gather the grapes; for the worms shall eat them."

1.12.3.en: St. Jerome uses this phrase with other passages of Holy Scripture to make clear that there is nothing in this world that can satisfy the depths of man. He says: [We must not seek the lust of possessions and money; it is written in Solomon, in the Book of Ecclesiastes: "He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver" (Eccl 5:10). And in Proverbs: "He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it" (Prov 11:26). Also in Isaiah: "Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!" (Isa 5:8). And also in Zephaniah: "They shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof; for the day of the LORD is near" (Zeph 1:13-14). And in the Gospel according to Luke: "For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?" (Lk 9:25)].

1.12.4.en: * Concerning that day the prophet Amos says: "Woe unto you that desire the day of the LORD! to what end is it for you? the day of the LORD is darkness, and not light" (Amos 5:18). And the prophet Zephaniah says the same thing: "The voice of the day of the LORD is dreadful and bitter" (Zeph 1:14-15). This is the reason why the penitent person is presented to us seeking earnestly in his prayer that he may not be judged for his works on that day of judgment. What is more profitable and far-sighted for a person than to pray for the fatherly love of God while he is still in this world, where there is opportunity for repentance, he who cannot have hope in his deserts because of the sins he has committed?

1.12.5.en: Cassiodorus * There is a light that can be perceived by the senses, of which it was said in Moses that it came into being on the fourth day, but it is not the true light, for it illumines the things that are on the earth. On the other hand, the Savior is the light of the spiritual world, for He shines upon the rational and the thinking, that their minds may see fitting visions. I mean that He is the light of the rational souls that are in the perceptible world, of whom the Savior teaches us that He is its Creator and its Director... He is the sun of the great day of the Lord.

1.13.s.en: 4. The great day of the Lord:

1.13.0.en: 14 "The great day of the LORD is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the LORD: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. 15 That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness, 16 A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities, and against the high towers. 17 And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the LORD: and their blood shall be poured out as dust, and their flesh as the dung. 18 Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD'S wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a sudden riddance of all them that dwell in the land."

1.13.1.en: The great day of the LORD is near.

1.13.2.en: It is near, and hasteth greatly.

1.13.3.en: Even the voice of the day of the LORD.

1.13.4.en: The mighty man shall cry there bitterly. [14]

1.13.5.en: Here the prophet gives a warning to Judah and Jerusalem of the nearness of the destruction that will befall by the Babylonians. It is not the day of the Babylonians, but "the great day of the LORD is near," for this destruction is only by the permission of the Lord to chasten them.

1.13.6.en: The prophet affirms that the day of chastening has become near and very swift; there is no time for slackness or postponement. Here, while he prophesies of the day of the captivity of Judah as the great day of the Lord, he also prophesies of the great day of judgment, when all mankind stand before the Lord.

1.13.7.en: These are very brief and repeated cries, for the danger is extremely grave and the time very short; there is no room for dialogue. It is like a man who sees his family inside the house and the fire beginning to blaze in it, so he cries out that perhaps all will hasten to go out by the nearest door or leap from the nearest window. And as was said by the prophet Amos: "The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither" (Amos 1:2).

1.13.8.en: This day began with the death of the good king Josiah, whom Pharaoh Necho killed at the battle of Megiddo, and the day continued until the destruction of Jerusalem was accomplished at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian.

1.13.9.en: The world's gold and silver cannot deliver us on the great day of the Lord, but the believer's wealth is the divine commandment; whoever keeps it, it keeps him from the divine wrath. The commandment is a treasure, which we acquire by the work of divine grace, so we bear the righteousness of Christ.

1.13.10.en: That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.

1.13.11.en: A day of wasteness and desolation.

1.13.12.en: A day of darkness and gloominess.

1.14.0.en: A day of clouds and thick darkness. [15]

1.14.1.en: The great day of the Lord is a day of joyful wedding for the believers who have prepared for the wedding through the riches of God's surpassing grace, and a day of wrath, distress, wasteness, desolation, darkness and gloominess for those who have not prepared for it by living faith working through love.

1.14.2.en: Human languages are no longer able to express the extent of the desolation that befalls Judah, so the prophet offers many synonyms that perhaps may depict the gravity of that day, so he calls it a day of wrath, as also a day of trouble and distress, of wasteness and desolation, of darkness and gloominess, of trumpet and alarm, and so on.

1.14.3.en: A grave picture, where the whirlwinds of divine wrath blow, so distress comes with total desolation, and all become like people in darkness, with no one having insight to see a way of salvation, and no one able to offer useful counsel. It is a day of dense cloud and fog that no man can resist or face.

1.15.0.en: A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities, and against the high towers. [16]

1.15.1.en: What citadel or fortress or walls can stand in the face of God's wrath? Those who think they are hidden in fortified cities and high towers hear the sounds of the trumpets of war and the shouts of the hostile armies, so their whole being collapses and their strength dissolves!

1.16.0.en: And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the LORD: and their blood shall be poured out as dust, and their flesh as the dung. [17]

1.16.1.en: The wicked on the great day of the Lord will be like the blind, for they are unable to enjoy the splendor of God's glory; they see God as a mighty Judge, not as a heavenly Bridegroom who gives His people fellowship in glory with Him.

1.16.2.en: Those who walk in evil, and resist the truth, and do not hearken to the voice of the Lord and His commandment are like blind men groping here and there, always in doubt and in danger! They search for a way of escape, but because of the blindness of their insight they do not see an escape that would save them.

1.16.3.en: Everything they touch and are certain of is that the sword strikes among them and their blood bursts forth, and their bodies fall under the feet of the enemy, with no one to bind up a wound and no one to lift a corpse from the dust!

1.17.0.en: Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD'S wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a sudden riddance of all them that dwell in the land. [18]

1.17.1.en: As they kindle the fire of divine jealousy by their disobedience and their abominations and their resistance to God, destruction befalls all, and the blow strikes the whole earth, so there is no hidden place in it to which anyone may flee. Here all the wealth they acquired unjustly cannot protect them from destruction. And as the wise man says: "Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death" (Prov 11:4).

1.17.2.en: * I am anxious and troubled as I speak of the multitude of ornaments; and I am obliged to be astonished how those who bear such a weight are not troubled by death. What a toil full of folly! What an absurd madness is exposed...! The rich man, as he fills his barns, says to his soul: "Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry." And behold, the Lord in the Gospels plainly calls him: "Thou fool" (Lk 12:20), "this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?" When the painter Apelles saw one of his pupils painting a picture of a person laden with a golden color to present it to Helen, he said to him: "Boy, since you are unable to paint her beautiful, you have painted her rich." Concerning these the prophet Zephaniah says: "Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD'S wrath" (Zeph 1:18). For it is fitting for these women who are being trained under the hands of Christ not to adorn themselves with gold but with the Word, through whom alone gold appears in the light.

1.17.3.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * Let us show the perfection of the obedience that is inspired in us by the expectation of His coming. Let us not hasten as slaves hasten, and defend ourselves before the Lord in a shameful and disgraceful manner. Rather let us persevere and strive and watch with all our hearts, and stand firm to the end. Let us keep the commandments of the Lord so that when the day of wrath and vengeance comes we may not be punished with the sinners and the wicked, but may be honored with the righteous and those who fear the Lord.

1.17.7.en: When will Your great day come?

1.17.8.en: Truly, the wicked man thinks that all the days are his day, so he acts arrogantly, and the righteous man groans, awaiting the day of Your great coming.

1.17.9.en: When will You come and support every soul in the midst of its groaning?

1.17.10.en: * You promised that You are coming quickly to chasten.

1.17.11.en: Chasten me in Your mercy, before Your coming on the clouds.

1.17.12.en: For I cannot flee from You, but I flee to You.

1.17.13.en: You are my refuge; I take shelter in You, so that wrath may not befall me!

1.17.14.en: If I ascend into heaven, You are there; and if I go down to Hades, I find You before me.

1.17.15.en: I flee to You, O Heavenly One.

1.17.16.en: Remove from me everything earthly by Your fiery Spirit.

1.17.17.en: So I shall become a second heaven for You, which destruction will not approach!

1.17.18.en: * May Your great day come now, for I know that You destroy in me everything that is evil, and cover me with Your righteousness and holiness!

1.17.19.en: * I await the coming of Your great last day!

1.17.20.en: I see You as the radiant Bridegroom, not the fearful Judge!

1.17.21.en: I see Your eyes as doves, but the wicked see them as burning fire.

1.17.22.en: The day of Your coming is a day of light and splendor, not a day of darkness and gloominess.

1.17.23.en: Your coming is the constant desire of my heart, and not a day of trouble and distress, wasteness and desolation.

1.17.24.en: Come on the clouds, and take me with You, that I may enter with You into the bosom of the Father!
